arbelos.definition: Curvilinear plane region bounded by three mutually tangent semicircles with collinear diameters AB = AC + CB on the same side of line AB; its area equals the circle whose diameter is the common internal tangent perpendicular CD (Book of Lemmas Prop. 4).
arbelos.archimedes_loci: Book of Lemmas Props. 4–6 (Heath 1897, pp. 304–308); Pappus IV.14

twin-circles.translation: equal circles inscribed in the partitioned arbelos
twin-circles.definition: The two circles inscribed on opposite sides of the perpendicular CD dividing the arbelos, each tangent to CD, the outer semicircle AB, and one inner semicircle (AC or CB); Archimedes proves they are strictly equal with radius r = (r1·r2)/(r1 + r2) (Book of Lemmas Prop. 5).

salinon.definition: Symmetric curvilinear figure formed by four semicircles on collinear segments with AD = EB: an outer semicircle AB and central opposite semicircle DE bridged by two inward equal semicircles AD, EB; its area equals the circle on the axial symmetry segment CF (Book of Lemmas Prop. 14).

neusis.definition: Geometric construction inserting a line segment of given length between two given curves or lines such that the extended line 'verges' (νεύει) toward a given point; used by Archimedes to trisect an arbitrary angle (Book of Lemmas Prop. 8) and construct spiral tangents (On Spirals Props. 5–9).
neusis.archimedes_loci: On Spirals Props. 5–9 (pp. 156–161); Book of Lemmas Prop. 8 (p. 309)

kentron-barous.definition: Unique point of a plane figure or solid body such that if suspended therefrom it remains in equilibrium in any orientation; proved in Equilibrium of Planes I.13–14 to coincide for any triangle with the concurrency of its medians (Kimberling center X(2)).
kentron-barous.archimedes_loci: Equilibrium I Post. 1–7, Props. 13–14 (pp. 189–202); Method Postulates

isorropia.definition: State in which magnitudes suspended at distances along a lever balance one another about a fulcrum; governed by Archimedes' seven postulates of plane statics.

antipeponthos.definition: Fundamental law proved for both commensurable (I.6) and incommensurable (I.7) magnitudes: two magnitudes balance at distances reciprocally proportional to their weights (A : B = d_B : d_A).
antipeponthos.archimedes_loci: Equilibrium of Planes I.6–7 (pp. 192–194); Method Prop. 1

ephodion.definition: Archimedes' analytic art of investigating unknown areas, volumes, and centroids by decomposing figures into parallel line or plane elements and balancing them on a virtual lever against known comparison solids prior to synthetic proof by exhaustion.

archimedes-lemma.definition: Of unequal lines, unequal surfaces, and unequal solids, the greater exceeds the less by such a magnitude as, when added to itself, can be made to exceed any assigned magnitude among those which are comparable with one another (credited by Archimedes to earlier geometers / Eudoxus; formalized as Hilbert Axiom V 1).
archimedes-lemma.archimedes_loci: Sphere & Cyl. I Assump. 5 (p. 4); Spirals Pref.; Quadrature Pref. (p. 234)

concave-same-way.headword: epi ta auta koila (ἐπὶ τὰ αὐτὰ κοῖλα)
concave-same-way.definition: Rigorous geometric definition of convexity for curves and surfaces in Sphere and Cylinder I: a curve or surface is concave in the same direction if the segment joining any two points on it lies wholly on one side (or on) the curve/surface, guaranteeing that an included convex perimeter/surface is strictly less than the enveloping one.
concave-same-way.archimedes_loci: Sphere & Cylinder I Defs. & Assump. 1–4 (Heath 1897, pp. 2–4)

exhaustion.definition: Rigorous Greek proof paradigm compressing an unknown curvilinear magnitude X between inscribed and circumscribed rectilinear/polygonal sequences (P_n < X < Q_n with Q_n - P_n < ε or Q_n / P_n < 1 + ε) and refuting both X > M and X < M by double reductio ad absurdum.
exhaustion.archimedes_loci: Measurement Prop. 1; Quadrature Props. 20–24; Sphere & Cyl. I.33–34

helix.definition: Plane kinematic locus traced by a point moving uniformly along a straight ray while the ray revolves uniformly in a plane about its fixed extremity O (polar equation r = aθ).

subtangent.greek: ἡ πρὸς ὀρθὰς τᾷ ἀρχᾷ τᾶς περιφορᾶς
subtangent.definition: Segment cut off on the perpendicular to the radius vector at the origin by the tangent to the spiral; in On Spirals Props. 18–20 Archimedes proves that at the end of the n-th turn its length equals n times the circumference of the corresponding circle, achieving the kinematic rectification of the circle.

tmema-paraboles.headword: tmema orthogoniou konou tomes (τμῆμα ὀρθογωνίου κώνου τομῆς)
tmema-paraboles.definition: Region comprehended by a straight chord AC and a 'section of a right-angled cone' (Archimedes' pre-Apollonian term for a parabola); its area equals 4/3 of the inscribed triangle of greatest area having the same base AC and vertex B where the tangent is parallel to AC.

orthogonion-konoeides.definition: Solid generated by revolving a parabola about its axis; Archimedes proves any segment cut off by a plane equals 3/2 of the cone having the same base and axis (half of the enveloping cylinder).
orthogonion-konoeides.archimedes_loci: On Conoids and Spheroids Props. 21–22 (pp. 131–134); Method Prop. 4

amblygonion-konoeides.definition: Solid generated by revolving one branch of a hyperbola ('section of an obtuse-angled cone') about its transverse diameter.
amblygonion-konoeides.archimedes_loci: On Conoids and Spheroids Props. 25–26 (pp. 137–140); Method Prop. 5

sphairoeides.definition: Solid generated by revolving an ellipse ('section of an acute-angled cone') about its major axis (elongate/prolate spheroid, παραμᾶκες) or minor axis (flat/oblate spheroid, ἐπιπλατύ).
sphairoeides.archimedes_loci: On Conoids and Spheroids Defs. & Props. 27–32 (pp. 101, 140–150); Method Prop. 3

bicylinder.translation: intersection of two orthogonal equal cylinders
bicylinder.greek: τὸ ἐξ ἀμφοτέρων τῶν κυλίνδρων κοινὸν σχῆμα
bicylinder.definition: Solid common to two right circular cylinders inscribed in a cube with perpendicular intersecting axes; in the concluding theorem of The Method Archimedes discovers and proves that its volume equals 2/3 of the cube (16/3 r³), matching an exclusively planar cross-sectional square construction.

ungula.translation: wedge cut from a cylinder by an oblique plane
ungula.definition: Solid cut from a right circular cylinder inscribed in a rectangular prism by a plane through a diameter of one base and a parallel edge of the opposite face; Archimedes proves both mechanically (Prop. 12–13) and purely geometrically via triangular cross-sections (Prop. 14) that its volume is 1/6 of the prism (2/3 r²h).

semi-regular-polyhedra.translation: vertex-transitive polyhedra with regular faces of two or three kinds
semi-regular-polyhedra.greek: τρισκαίδεκα σχήματα ἰσόπλευρα μὲν καὶ ἰσογώνια, οὐχ ὅμοια δέ
semi-regular-polyhedra.definition: The complete finite family of 13 convex non-prismatic, non-Platonic polyhedra bounded by regular polygons of two or three species meeting in congruent vertex configurations, discovered by Archimedes and catalogued in Pappus's Synagoge V.19.
semi-regular-polyhedra.archimedes_loci: Pappus Synagoge V.19; Heath 1897 Ch. V; Pacioli De Divina Proportione

myriad-octads.translation: orders and periods of large numbers
myriad-octads.definition: Positional naming system constructed in The Sand-Reckoner taking 10^8 (a myriad myriads) as the base of successive 'orders' up to the (10^8)-th order (First Period = 10^(8·10^8)) and iterating through 10^8 Periods up to 10^(8·10^16), accompanied by the law of exponents A_m · A_n = A_(m+n-1).

stomachion.definition: Combinatorial and areal dissection of a 12 × 12 square into 14 rational-area polygonal tiles (areas 3, 6, 9, 12, 14, 21 out of 144) admitting 17,152 (536 distinct modulo dihedral symmetry) square assemblies.
stomachion.archimedes_loci: Heiberg Vol. II (1913, pp. 416–424); Palimpsest fol. 177

quadrea.definition: Symmetric quadratic polynomial A(Q1, Q2, Q3) = (Q1 + Q2 + Q3)^2 - 2(Q1^2 + Q2^2 + Q3^2) = 16·Area^2 in the three side quadrances of a triangle (attributed to Archimedes via Arabic Heron tradition and central to Rational Trigonometry in geometor/wildberger).
quadrea.archimedes_loci: geometor/wildberger; Book of Lemmas & Heron Metrica I.8
